title: Running Pace: min/km vs min/mile — Full Conversion Table
h1: Running pace — min/km vs min/mile and the 1.609 factor
description: 5:00/km = 8:03/mile. Convert training pace, race splits and marathon targets between km and mile with the exact 1.609344 factor.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against BIPM SI Brochure, IAAF/World Athletics course measurement rules and Daniels' Running Formula (3rd ed.)

hero: A 5:00/km pace is 8:03/mile — the mile is 1.609344 km, so pace-per-mile is always slower-looking by that same factor. Get the mapping wrong at marathon distance and a 3:30 goal quietly becomes a 3:35 finish.
body: Pace is time per distance, so the conversion is the inverse of the distance factor. 1 mile = 1.609344 km exactly (defined by the international yard and pound agreement of 1959, adopted by NIST SP 811). To convert min/km to min/mile, multiply by 1.609344. To convert the other way, divide. That is it — every pace chart in every running book uses this one number.

> min/mile = min/km × 1.609344
> min/km = min/mile ÷ 1.609344
> Speed (kph) = 60 ÷ (min/km)
> Speed (mph) = 60 ÷ (min/mile)
> Reference: 1 mile = 1609.344 m (NIST SP 811, §B.8)

Because a marathon is 42.195 km = 26.219 miles (World Athletics Rule 240), a target time maps directly to pace. A 3:30 marathon is 210 min ÷ 42.195 km = 4:59/km = 8:01/mile. A 3:00 goal is 4:16/km = 6:52/mile. Elite men run about 2:52/km (4:37/mile); the current world record (Kelvin Kiptum, Chicago 2023, 2:00:35) averages 2:51.6/km = 4:36.3/mile.

A runner training in km sets a 5:00/km goal for a marathon and books a US race that publishes pace bands in min/mile. They line up behind the 8:00/mile pacer, thinking it is 'about the same'. Actual pace: 8:00/mile = 4:58.4/km — 1.6 seconds/km faster. Over 42.195 km that is +67 seconds, so goal 3:30:44 → finish 3:31:51. In the other direction (following the 8:10/mile pacer for a 5:00/km target), the runner ends up 3:37:20 — five minutes off. The 1.609 factor is small in feel, huge over the distance.

Modern GPS watches (Garmin Forerunner, Coros Pace 3, Apple Watch Ultra) let you switch pace units per activity — set it to match the race, not your training preference. Treadmills sold in the US show mph and min/mile; European gyms show kph and min/km. A treadmill set to 12.0 kph = 5:00/km = 8:03/mile = 7.46 mph. The treadmill's own conversion is rounded to 0.1 mph, so 12.0 kph often displays as 7.5 mph — expect a 3–5 second/mile display error.

Strava, Garmin and TrainingPeaks show grade-adjusted pace to compare hilly to flat efforts. The standard model (based on Alberto Minetti's 2002 energy-cost curves, *J. Appl. Physiol.* 93:1039–1046) adds roughly 12–15 seconds/km per 1% incline at moderate paces, and returns 6–8 seconds/km per 1% decline. Convert the flat-equivalent pace with 1.609344 the same way — GAP is a pace, not a separate unit.
min/mile = min/km × 1.609344. Round only for display. Marathon 3:30 = 4:59/km = 8:01/mile. Always sanity-check pacer bands before a race in the other unit system.

faqs.a: The mile was fixed at exactly 1609.344 metres by the 1959 international yard and pound agreement (NIST SP 811, Appendix B). All modern conversions use the full value; 1.609 introduces a 0.02% rounding error — about 0.5 s over a 42.195 km marathon.

faqs.q: How do I convert kph to min/km in my head?
faqs.a: min/km = 60 ÷ kph. 12 kph = 5:00/km, 10 kph = 6:00/km, 15 kph = 4:00/km. Every whole kph between 8 and 20 gives a clean pace anchor.

faqs.q: Is my treadmill's pace display accurate?
faqs.a: Belt speed is usually within ±3% of display (ISO 20957-6 test tolerance). Add GPS or a footpod for training data; use the treadmill number for effort control only.

faqs.q: Do World Athletics records use km or miles?
faqs.a: Records are set at metric distances (5000 m, 10 000 m, marathon 42.195 km). The mile is one of the few imperial events still ratified — the world record (Hicham El Guerrouj, 3:43.13, 1999) equals 3:26.4/km = 5:32.5/mile average.

faqs.q: Why does my watch's average pace not match my split pace?
faqs.a: GPS smooths position over a 1–3 s window, so instantaneous pace lags. Auto-lap averages across the lap and matches better; use lap pace for pacing decisions, not the live display.
